headline: Yields stood still, bond vol did not: MOVE up another 4.9% to 106.8 (z=2.8) while gold finally stopped falling and the dollar took over as the transmission channel.
summary: The shock changed venue today. Cash yields printed the same levels — 10y 5.24%, 2y 4.92%, 30y 5.56%, all at the 100th percentile of the last year — but the pressure moved into bond volatility. MOVE rose another 4.9% to 106.77, now +50.4% on the month with a 2.76 z-score and acceleration of 1.94, 45.6% above its 200-day. TLT fell 0.9% to 77.94 and sits at the 0th percentile, as do IEF and LQD. The 10-year real yield is 2.90%, +48bp in a month, 37% above its 200-day, with acceleration 1.39. The rates composite slipped again to -85 from -83; risk regime is unchanged at -15. This is the part of the move that costs money even when the index doesn't fall: collateral is repricing faster than prices.

The commodity leg flipped in two directions at once. Precious metals stopped bleeding — gold +0.3% to 4,179.6, GDX +0.4%, GDXJ +0.2%, NEM +0.7% — after a week in which GDX lost 9.8% and GDXJ 10.6% with acceleration z-scores of -3.26 and -2.97. That is what a washout print looks like. Industrial hard assets did not join: XME -1.9% (-12.8% on the month, acceleration -2.42), FCX -2.1%, COPX -0.5%, even though copper itself rose 0.6% and copper/gold sits at the 96.7th percentile. Energy cracked: Brent -7.7% to 97.17, WTI -2.0% to 90.74, RBOB -5.5% and -9.6% on the month. Breakevens did not move — 5y 2.33%, 10y 2.34% — so the entire yield surge remains real, not inflationary. Cheaper crude plus a flat breakeven is relief for the consumer and a problem for the last cyclical bid.

The dollar is now doing the damage. DXY +0.3% to 101.53 with acceleration 1.12, +1.8% on the month; EURUSD -0.5% to 1.1322 at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range with acceleration -1.88; USDCHF +0.7% to a fresh 52-week high (z=1.88); AUDUSD -0.6%, AUDJPY -3.7% on the month. The clean tell: local European indices were fine — Euro Stoxx +0.3%, DAX +0.1% — while their dollar versions were not: EWP -1.7%, EWU -1.4%, EWI -1.2%, EWG -1.0%, EFA -1.0%. Asia was worse in its own currency: KOSPI -2.7%, Shanghai -1.7%, KWEB -1.7%, FXI -1.3%. USDMXN's five-day panic paused (+0.1%), but that is the only place the dollar squeeze eased.

Inside the US the index keeps lying. SPX -0.3% to 7,658.9, still 6.1% above its 200-day at the 90th percentile; NDX flat. Leadership narrowed further into AI hardware: SMH +1.1%, SOXX +1.1% and +11.5% on the month, ASML +2.6%, AVGO +1.9%, MU +1.2%, SMH/SPY z=1.35. Everything rate-sensitive lost ground: KRE and KBE both -1.2%, ITB -1.2% with the 30-year mortgage at 7.03% (+38bp on the month), XHB/SPY at the 2nd percentile. Breadth made a new cycle low — RSP/SPY z=-2.15 at the 7th percentile, IWM/SPY -5.3% on the month, IYT/SPY at the 5th percentile. The consumer tape is ugly in the megacaps: WMT -2.8%, MCD -10.8% on the month (z=-2.33, 1st percentile), HD at the 0th percentile. The genuinely new information is credit: HYG -0.4% with z=-1.67 and acceleration -1.39, rolling over, while HYG/IEF still sits at the 94th percentile. Spreads have not yet paid for what duration already has. VIX at 16.15 is in the 15th percentile — but VIX/VIX3M turned up to 0.891 with acceleration 1.54.

good.text: The precious-metals liquidation looks exhausted: gold +0.3% to 4,179.6 after a -4.5% week, GDX +0.4%, GDXJ +0.2%, NEM +0.7%, with acceleration z-scores of -3.26, -2.97 and -3.19 — three-sigma capitulation followed by a green print.

AI hardware leadership widened rather than cracked: SMH +1.1%, SOXX +1.1% (+11.5% on the month), ASML +2.6%, MU +1.2%, TSM +0.8%, SMH/SPY z=1.35 and +10.3% relative in a month. Taiwan's TAIEX sits at the 99th percentile.
Energy relief for the consumer and for breakevens: Brent -7.7% to 97.17, WTI -2.0%, RBOB -5.5% and -9.6% on the month, while 5-year breakevens sit at 2.33% in the 30th percentile.

The growth pulse still reads +16, not a recession: copper +0.6%, copper/gold at the 96.7th percentile, XLI/XLU at the 96.6th, high-beta/low-vol at the 97.2nd. This is a discount-rate event, not a demand event.
No default stress yet: HYG/IEF is still at the 94th percentile, BKLN unchanged on the day and +0.4% on the month at the 92nd percentile. The pain is duration and leverage, not solvency.
Crypto keeps absorbing a rising dollar: BTC 82,920 (+6.8% on the month, +41.6% on three), ETH +10.5% monthly, SOL +15.5%, all with trend states turning up despite DXY at the 98th percentile.

bad.text: Bond volatility is accelerating into the move, not fading: MOVE +4.9% to 106.77, +50.4% on the month, z=2.76 with acceleration 1.94 and 45.6% above its 200-day. Faster, not calmer — that is a tightening, not a repricing.
The 10-year real yield at 2.90% is +48bp in a month (z=1.89, acceleration 1.39) and 37% above its 200-day, with breakevens flat at 2.34%. Every basis point is real cost of capital.

Breadth made a new cycle low: RSP/SPY z=-2.15 at the 7th percentile, IWM/SPY -5.3% on the month, IYT/SPY at the 5th percentile, DJT -8.5% monthly. The S&P is 6.1% above its 200-day on a shrinking base.

Credit is starting to join: HYG -0.4% with z=-1.67 and acceleration -1.39, rolling over; LQD and IEF both at the 0th percentile. Yet HYG/IEF is still at the 94th percentile — the risk premium has not repriced at all.

The dollar is now the pain channel: DXY acceleration 1.12, EURUSD at the 0th percentile with acceleration -1.88, USDCHF at a 52-week high. Euro Stoxx +0.3% locally but EWP -1.7%, EWU -1.4%, EFA -1.0% in dollars.

Rate-sensitive domestic demand keeps deteriorating: 30-year mortgage 7.03% (+38bp on the month), ITB -1.2% and -8.2% monthly, HD at the 0th percentile after -12.2%, MCD z=-2.33 at the 1st percentile, WMT -2.8%.

trades.name: Own equity vol against bond vol
trades.line: Buy SPY Nov puts / VIX calls: VIX 16 vs MOVE 107
trades.expr: Buy SPY Nov 745 puts (~2% OTM), partially financed by selling Nov 700s; or VIX Nov 20 calls. Size 50-75bp premium.
trades.thesis: Bond vol at a 2.76 z-score with 1.94 acceleration has never coexisted for long with a 16 VIX in the 15th percentile. The index is 6.1% above its 200-day while breadth sits at a cycle low; the gap closes through the index, and the cheapest way to own that is listed vol.
trades.trigger: MOVE +4.9% to 106.77 (+50.4% on the month) while VIX printed just 16.15; VIX/VIX3M turned up to 0.891 with acceleration 1.54; RSP/SPY z=-2.15 at the 7th percentile.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.85 with MOVE under 95 — the rates shock is over and carry kills the position.
trades.target: VIX 22-24, SPY toward 730 (-4%); take half on the first VIX print above 21.

trades.name: Short HYG vs long IEF
trades.line: Short HYG vs IEF: spread 94th pct while HYG acc is -1.39
trades.expr: Short HYG, long IEF in equal dollars (or buy HYG Dec 76 puts outright for convexity).
trades.thesis: Duration has fully repriced — LQD and IEF at the 0th percentile — but the credit risk premium has not: HYG/IEF still sits at the 94th percentile. If the real-yield shock keeps grinding on leveraged balance sheets, that ratio mean-reverts before defaults ever appear.
trades.trigger: HYG -0.4% to 77.22 with z=-1.67 and acceleration -1.39, trend rolling over; BX -20.0% on the month (z=-2.06), GS -11.8%, KRE -1.2% on the day.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF closes above 0.874 (new cycle high) — the spread simply refuses to widen.
trades.target: HYG/IEF to 0.840, roughly -2.9% on the ratio.

trades.name: Long SMH vs short KRE
trades.line: Long semis vs regional banks: capex bid vs a 4.92% 2-year
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long SMH, short KRE. Roll monthly.
trades.thesis: Two ways to own the same rates shock: the AI complex is funded by cash flow and keeps making relative highs; regional banks are funded by a 2-year at 4.92% with 2s10s flattened to 32bp. The tape is paying for the first and charging for the second every single day.
trades.trigger: SMH +1.1% and SOXX +11.5% on the month with SMH/SPY z=1.35, against KRE -1.2% (-5.7% monthly) and KRE/SPY at the 28th percentile; 2s10s flattened 4bp to 32bp.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY closes below its 200-day, or the pair drawdown exceeds 8%.
trades.target: +10-12% on the pair; exit if the 2-year drops 40bp and the curve re-steepens.

trades.name: Gold miners into the washout
trades.line: Buy GDX after 3-sigma capitulation; gold held 4,180
trades.expr: Long GDX outright, half size, add GDXJ on confirmation; or Nov 95 calls to define risk.
trades.thesis: A -9.8% week in GDX with acceleration at -3.26 and GDX/gold at -3.03 is forced selling, not a thesis change. Gold is 8.3% below its 200-day at a -1.87 z-score. The first green day after that profile is usually tradable even inside a real-yield uptrend.
trades.trigger: Gold +0.3% to 4,179.6 and GDX +0.4%, GDXJ +0.2%, NEM +0.7% — the first positive close after the flush.
trades.stop: Gold below 4,050 or GDX below 82 on a close; real yields through 3.00% would extend the pain.

trades.name: Short EUR/USD
trades.expr: Short EURUSD spot or 6E futures; or long UUP as a proxy. 1% risk to the 1.1450 stop.
trades.thesis: The dollar is being pulled higher by a 2.90% US real yield, and the euro is the funding casualty. Local European equity is fine — the currency is doing all the damage, which is exactly how these trends extend rather than exhaust.
trades.trigger: EURUSD -0.5% to 1.1322, 0th percentile of the 52-week range with acceleration -1.88; DXY +0.3% with acceleration 1.12; USDCHF at a fresh 52-week high (z=1.88).
trades.stop: 1.1450 on a close — that breaks the acceleration and the 2.6% gap to the 200-day.

trades.name: Short home construction
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.03% mortgage, XHB/SPY at the 2nd percentile
trades.expr: Short ITB, or Dec 85 puts; pair against long SPY if you want the beta out.
trades.thesis: There is no housing recovery with a 7.03% mortgage and a 10-year at 5.24%. Builders are already 9.2% below the 200-day and making new relative lows, and the spillover is visible in HD at the 0th percentile — the consumer half of the trade is confirming.
trades.trigger: Mortgage 7.03%, +38bp on the month (z=1.14); ITB -1.2% today, -8.2% monthly, 8th percentile; XHB/SPY at the 2nd percentile; DHI -0.7%.
trades.stop: 10-year back below 5.00% or ITB above 93 on a close.

trades.name: Short oil services
trades.line: Short OIH: Brent -7.7%, RBOB -9.6% on the month
trades.expr: Short OIH; or pair long XLE / short OIH to isolate capex from reserves.
trades.thesis: Services need a high and rising strip to justify a capex cycle. Crude just broke while the product crack has been collapsing for a month, and OIH has already lost its relative-strength trend — the equity is de-rating ahead of the commodity.
trades.trigger: Brent -7.7% to 97.17 and WTI -2.0% to 90.74; RBOB -5.5% today, -9.6% on the month (z=-0.99); OIH -1.6%, -8.3% monthly with acceleration -1.30 and relative strength rolling over versus XLE's +14.2% three-month lead.
trades.stop: Brent back above 103 or OIH above 400 on a close.
